extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of Perelman's monotone functionals (F, W, λ, µ, ν), their first-variation and monotonicity under coupled Ricci–heat flows, and Hamilton's maximum principles for scalar/tensor quantities in Ricci flow. Aimed at understanding analytic tools used to rule out nontrivial breathers and to preserve curvature positivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of breather
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition 1.5.1: A metric gij(t) evolving by the Ricci flow is called a breather if for some t1 < t2 and α > 0 the metrics α g_{ij}(t1) and g_{ij}(t2) differ only by a diffeomorphism; α = 1, α < 1, α > 1 correspond to steady, shrinking and expanding breathers, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Ricci solitons (steady, shrinking, expanding) are trivial breathers for which the relationship (diffeomorphism + scaling) holds for every pair of times t1,t2. Breatherness corresponds to a periodic orbit in metric space modulo diffeomorphism and scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's F-functional
rubrics_metrics.description: F(g_{ij},f) = ∫_M (R + |∇f|^2) e^{-f} dV defined on Riemannian metrics and smooth functions f on M (Equation (1.5.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domain: compact n-manifold M; R is scalar curvature. The functional is used to detect gradient solitons and to obtain monotonic quantities under coupled flows of g and f.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation of F
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 1.5.2 (Perelman): If δg_{ij} = v_{ij} and δf = h, then the first variation δF(v_{ij},h) is given by an integral formula involving v_{ij}(R_{ij}+∇_i∇_j f), the trace v, and h (explicit formula stated in Lemma 1.5.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This first-variation formula identifies the Euler–Lagrange equation for minimizers and is used to compute evolution of F under coupled flows. Keep track of normalization v = g^{ij} v_{ij} and the weight e^{-f}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of F under coupled flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 1.5.3 (Perelman): Under the coupled flow ∂_t g_{ij} = -2R_{ij} and ∂_t f = -∆f + |∇f|^2 - R, one has d/dt F(g(t),f(t)) = 2 ∫_M |R_{ij} + ∇_i∇_j f|^2 e^{-f} dV; hence F is nondecreasing in time and monotonicity is strict unless on a steady gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: equality (no increase) characterizes steady gradient solitons. The explicit squared-integrand yields a Lyapunov-type monotonicity formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: λ-energy definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition (1.5.6): λ(g_{ij}) = inf_{f, ∫_M e^{-f} dV = 1} F(g_{ij},f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, with u = e^{-f/2} and ∫_M u^2 dV = 1, λ is the first eigenvalue of the operator -4∆ + R. A minimizer u_0 (positive) satisfies -4∆u_0 + Ru_0 = λ(g) u_0 and f_0 = -2 log u_0 minimizes F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity and rigidity for λ
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.5.4: λ(g(t)) is nondecreasing along Ricci flow and monotonicity is strict unless on a steady gradient soliton; furthermore any steady breather is a steady gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: λ(g) is invariant under diffeomorphism; monotonicity is proved by solving backward heat equation for f and comparing F-values. Use this to rule out nontrivial steady breathers on compact manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale-invariant ¯λ and expanding case
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ¯λ(g) = λ(g) V(g)^{2/n} where V is volume. Corollary 1.5.5: ¯λ(g(t)) is nondecreasing along Ricci flow whenever it is nonpositive, with strict monotonicity unless on a gradient expanding soliton; an expanding breather is necessarily an expanding gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: combine volume evolution, choice of backward solution f(t), and Cauchy–Schwarz to obtain monotonicity in the expanding regime; invariance under scaling/diffeomorphism is essential for treating expanding breathers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steady/expanding breathers are Einstein on compact manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 1.5.6: On a compact manifold, a steady or expanding breather is necessarily an Einstein metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine previous monotonicity and rigidity corollaries with Proposition (1.1.1) to deduce that compact steady or expanding Ricci solitons must be gradient and then Einstein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's W-functional
rubrics_metrics.guidance: W is invariant under simultaneous scaling of τ and g (parabolic scaling) and under diffeomorphism: W(a ϕ^* g, ϕ^* f, a τ) = W(g,f,τ). W is tailored to study shrinking solitons and yields the µ/ν-energies.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation of W
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 1.5.7 (Perelman): For variations v_{ij}=δg_{ij}, h=δf, η=δτ, δW(v,h,η) has an explicit integral formula involving τ(R_{ij}+∇_i∇_j f), the trace v, h, and η (formula stated in lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to identify critical points (shrinking solitons) and to compute evolution under coupled flows including τ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of W under coupled g,f,τ flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 1.5.8: If ∂_t g_{ij} = -2R_{ij}, ∂_t f = -∆f + |∇f|^2 - R + n/(2τ), and ∂_t τ = -1, then d/dt W(g(t),f(t),τ(t)) = 2τ ∫ |R_{ij} + ∇_i∇_j f - (1/2τ) g_{ij}|^2 (4π τ)^{-n/2} e^{-f} dV, so W is nondecreasing and equality holds exactly on shrinking gradient solitons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: W is a Lyapunov functional for the backward-in-time coupled flow with τ decreasing; vanishing of the integrand characterizes shrinking solitons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of µ and ν energies
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions (1.5.12): µ(g,τ) = inf_{f, (4π τ)^{-n/2} ∫ e^{-f} dV = 1} W(g,f,τ). ν(g) = inf_{τ>0} µ(g,τ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: µ(g,τ) corresponds to the best constant in a logarithmic Sobolev inequality; minimizers exist (regularity via Euler–Lagrange), satisfy τ(2∆f - |∇f|^2 + R) + f - n = µ(g,τ). µ and ν are used to control shrinking behavior and to obtain rigidity statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity and rigidity for µ
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary 1.5.9: µ(g(t), τ(t)) is nondecreasing along Ricci flow (with τ appropriately chosen backward) and monotonicity is strict unless on a shrinking gradient soliton; a shrinking breather is necessarily a shrinking gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy parallels that for F/λ: choose minimizer at t0, solve backward heat equation for f, use invariances to compare W-values, and deduce equality implies soliton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion function with controlled derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.1.1: There exists a smooth function f on M with f ≥ 1 everywhere, f(x) → ∞ as d_0(x,x_0) → ∞, and bounds |∇ f| ≤ C, |∇^2 f| ≤ C (uniform in space-time) for metrics gij(t) evolving by Ricci flow with bounded curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: mollification via local coordinate exponential map and use of Hessian comparison + Shi derivative estimates to ensure bounds persist under the evolving metric. Such an f is used as barrier in maximum-principle arguments on noncompact manifolds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of nonnegativity of scalar curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.2: If scalar curvature R ≥ 0 at t=0 for a Ricci flow solution with bounded curvature on [0,T], then R ≥ 0 on M × [0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses barrier function ε e^{At} f added to R and the scalar evolution ∂_t R = ∆R + 2|Ric|^2, then apply weak maximum principle. Choose A large so that the modified quantity satisfies the parabolic inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle for tensors (weak form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.1.3: Suppose ∂_t M_{αβ} = ∆M_{αβ} + u^i ∇_i M_{αβ} + N_{αβ} on [0,T], where u^i bounded and N_{αβ} = P(M_{αβ}, h_{αβ}) is a polynomial in M_{αβ} (contracted with the bundle metric) satisfying P-condition: N_{αβ} v^α v^β ≥ 0 whenever M_{αβ} v^α = 0. If M_{αβ} ≥ 0 at t=0 then M_{αβ} ≥ 0 for all t∈[0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: add ε e^{At} f h_{αβ} to M, choose A large, use argument at first null vector (extension by parallel transport) and contradiction. This is the tensor analogue of scalar maximum principle and a building block for curvature preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of nonnegativity of curvature operator
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.4 (Hamilton): Nonnegativity of the curvature operator M_{αβ} is preserved by Ricci flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Lemma 2.1.3 to the curvature operator evolution ∂_t M = ∆M + M^2 + M^# to conclude M≥0 is preserved. Use bounded curvature hypotheses as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of nonnegativity of holomorphic bisectional curvature in Kähler case
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition 2.1.5: Under the Kähler-Ricci flow, if the initial metric has positive (or nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature then the evolved metric also has positive (or nonnegative) holomorphic bisectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: Bando (n=3), Mok (compact general n), Shi (noncompact). The statement is an application of tensor maximum principles adapted to Kähler geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hamilton's strong maximum principle for tensors
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.2.1: For M_{αβ} evolving by ∂_t M = ∆M + N(M) on a bounded connected open set Ω with N polynomial of M and N≥0 whenever M≥0, if M_{αβ} ≥ 0 initially then there exists δ>0 so that on Ω × (0,δ) the rank of M_{αβ} is constant, the null space of M_{αβ} is invariant under parallel translation and in time, and the null space lies in the null space of N_{αβ}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a local positivity function ρ evolved by heat equation, an εe^{t} perturbation, extension of orthonormal vectors by parallel transport, and contradiction at first touching time. Consequence: rigidity of the null space structure under the flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of curvature operator is Lie subalgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.2.2 (Hamilton): If initial curvature operator M_{αβ} is nonnegative, then for some time interval (0,δ) the image of M_{αβ} is a Lie subalgebra of so(n) of constant rank, invariant under parallel translation and in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: apply strong maximum principle to curvature operator and analyze M^# terms; deduce structure constants C^ξγ_α vanish appropriately so that image is closed under Lie bracket. Links to holonomy via Ambrose–Singer theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced maximum principle (Hamilton)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 2.3.1: Let V be a vector bundle with time-dependent connection ∇_t and bundle metric h (time-independent). Let K⊂V be closed, invariant under parallel translation (H1), and with convex fiber-intersections K_x (H2). Suppose the fiber ODE dσ_x/dt = N(x,σ_x,t) preserves each K_x. Then any uniformly bounded solution σ(x,t) of the PDE ∂_t σ = ∆_t σ + u^i ∇_i σ + N(x,σ,t) that starts in K at t0 remains in K for all later times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem reduces PDE preservation problems to ODE preservation in each fiber: check invariance/convexity of K and that ODE trajectories starting in K_x stay in K_x. Lemma 2.1.3 is a special case (K = nonnegative symmetric forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison lemma for Lipschitz functions (Gronwall-type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.3.2: If ϕ : [a,b] → R is Lipschitz and dϕ/dt ≤ C ϕ(t) whenever ϕ(t) > 0, and ϕ(a) ≤ 0, then ϕ(t) ≤ 0 on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard device to propagate sign information using differential inequalities; used to show distances to convex sets remain zero (hence containment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative bound for sup-functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.3.3: For ψ(x,t) smooth on X×[a,b] and Y⊂X compact, define ϕ(t)=sup_{y∈Y} ψ(y,t). Then forward derivative dϕ/dt(t) ≤ sup_{y∈Y, ψ(y,t)=ϕ(t)} ∂ψ/∂t (y,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate time derivative of a supremum (or distance function) to pointwise time derivatives at maximizers; instrumental in reducing PDE to ODE estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of ODE preserving a convex set
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 2.3.4: For ODE dϕ/dt = N(ϕ,t) on open U⊂R^n and closed convex Z⊂U, the following are equivalent: (i) solutions starting in Z remain in Z; (ii) for every ϕ∈∂Z and t, ϕ + N(ϕ,t) ∈ T_ϕ Z (the tangent cone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalence is proved by support function/tangent cone analysis and using Lemma 2.3.3 plus a Lipschitz bound. This lemma is the finite-dimensional core used in Hamilton's advanced maximum principle to check ODE invariance of fibers.
